what_happened: The ego was about 4 m left of the recorded route, one lane over. It followed slower actor 87 in that lane and closed the gap from 14.4 m to 2.5 m over 2 s while only easing from 6.8 to 5.1 m/s, then hit 87 with its front. The planned path ran straight into 87 even though the route said RIGHT; 87 looked smeared on camera but was still clearly a car.

On a multi-lane freeway with a RIGHT command, the ego was driving one lane left of the recorded path, and a much slower actor 87 was directly ahead in that lane. The ego closed the gap from 13.4 m to 3.7 m while easing off only from 7.4 to 6.0 m/s, and its front hit 87 at 10.1 s. The camera image of 87 was heavily smeared, but a car-shaped object was clearly visible ahead the whole time, so the rendering doesn't excuse the weak braking. The later rear contact came after this front collision.

On the multi-lane highway the ego drifted about one lane left of the recorded path, despite a RIGHT command. It ended up behind actor 87 and ran into its rear at about 5 m/s: it slowed only gently (7.0→5.0 m/s) while the gap closed from 14.6 m to 3.3 m. The camera showed the lead car smeared but visible because the ego was off the recording; the rear contact came after the front collision.

After handoff on a multi-lane highway, the ego sped up from 4.4 to 6.5 m/s and drifted left toward the recorded human's lane-change path. It cut into the adjacent left lane while vehicle 56 was right there, slightly ahead, and its front hit 56. A rear contact is also flagged, but the front collision came first.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the ego sped up from 4.4 to 6.4 m/s after handoff. Over the same stretch it yawed left off its lane: the lane lines in the ego-centred map tilt more and more, and it ended 1.5 m off the recorded path. Its front-left hit actor 56, which was travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane, even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT.

After handoff, the ego sped up from about 4.4 to 6.5 m/s and drifted left out of its lane, moving about 3.3 m away from the recorded position. It moved into the left lane at actor 56, which was alongside and slightly ahead, and hit it with the ego's front at 7.2 s (the gap ahead dropped to 2.5 m).

On a multi-lane highway, the policy's planned path (orange) swung left toward the next lane, while the recorded route stayed in its lane. The ego sped up from 4.4 to 6.6 m/s as it drifted left and hit vehicle 56 with its front at 7.2 s; vehicle 56 was travelling alongside, slightly ahead in the left lane.

On a multi-lane highway at about 5 m/s, the route command changed to RIGHT, but the ego's planned path curved left instead and the ego drifted over the left lane line. A small actor (29, probably a motorcycle) was passing on the left from behind, and the ego's front-left corner hit it at 12.1 s.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego slowed to about 3–5 m/s with open road ahead (gap over 33 m) and its path drifted left toward the lane line, about 2.4 m off the human's recorded line, even though the route command was RIGHT. Actor 19, coming from behind on the left, then sideswiped the ego's left side.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego crawled at about 3.8 m/s while its plan bent left, off the green route line, so it ended up about 1.9 m off the recorded path and partly in the left lane. Actor 25, a faster vehicle coming up from behind in that lane, then struck the ego's front-left corner: the gap fell from 34 m to 2.1 m in half a second.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego crawled at about 3–4 m/s and drifted left, ending up about 1.9 m from the recorded path, which ran to its right. A small actor (id 29, probably a motorcycle) came up from behind in the left lane and hit the ego's left front side; the actor wasn't on the map at 10.6 s, and the collision was lateral, not front.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the ego was slowing (4.5 to 2.9 m/s) while its planned path bent left out of its lane, away from the straight route line. It drifted about 1.6 m left of the recorded trajectory and side-swiped actor 29, which was passing in the adjacent left lane (lateral collision).

On a multi-lane highway with a RIGHT command, the ego kept straddling the dashed line to its right and slowed from 4.7 to 3.4 m/s while the recorded car moved ahead and to the right. Replayed actor 9 came up from behind in the lane to the right and side-swiped the ego's rear right (lateral contact). Nothing was close ahead, so this was not a failure to brake for a lead vehicle.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego slowed to about 4 m/s and drifted left until it straddled the lane line, about 1.9 m off the recorded path. A motorcycle (actor 25) passing from behind on the left was in that space, and the ego's front-left clipped it at 12.1 s. In the real drive the ego stayed in its lane and the motorcycle went by safely, so the ego's lateral drift caused the collision.

The ego was going 3.5–4.6 m/s on a multi-lane highway, much slower than the recorded drive; by the failure it was about 70 m behind where the human car was. It had also drifted about 1.7 m left of the recorded path. A replayed vehicle (actor 2) that wasn't in view before came from behind/the left and ended up overlapping the ego's front-left corner at 11.6 s, so the gap to the vehicle ahead suddenly dropped from 34 m to 2.1 m. This is not a lead vehicle the ego ran into: the ego's crawl speed and leftward drift put it in the path of a vehicle that, in the original drive, would never have met it.
